battle_tutorial_ability_message_00100:
Take a look at the Greninja in the 
Active Spot.
battle_tutorial_ability_message_00200:
Abilities are special powers that Pokémon
have that are different from attacks.
battle_tutorial_ability_message_00300:
Unlike attacks, using an Ability does not
end your turn.
battle_tutorial_ability_message_00400: There are Abilities that work all the time.
battle_tutorial_ability_message_00500:
This Greninja has the 
Water Shuriken Ability.
battle_tutorial_ability_message_00600:
This powerful Ability lets you do damage 
in addition to its attack damage.
battle_tutorial_ability_message_00800:
You’ve attached an Energy, so use the
attack to Knock Out Jynx.
battle_tutorial_attack_message_00100:
Knock Out your opponent’s Pokémon to
earn points.
battle_tutorial_attack_message_00200:
If you’re the first to reach 3 points,
you win the battle.
battle_tutorial_attack_message_00400:
Use Pikachu’s Gnaw attack to Knock Out
your opponent’s Eevee.
battle_tutorial_bench_message_00100:
Start your turn by drawing a card from
your deck.
battle_tutorial_bench_message_00200:
You can play cards that are in your hand
during your turn.
battle_tutorial_bench_message_00300:
Play Pikachu from your hand to
your Bench.
battle_tutorial_bench_message_00400:
If you have no Pokémon left in play, you
lose the battle.
battle_tutorial_bench_message_00500:
But now, even if your Active Pokémon is
Knocked Out, you don’t need to worry!
battle_tutorial_bench_message_00600:
Eevee in the Active Spot was
Knocked Out.
battle_tutorial_bench_message_00700:
Choose a Benched Pokémon to move to
the Active Spot.
battle_tutorial_energy_active_message_00: Pokémon need Energy to use attacks.

When it is your turn, an Energy is
generated in the Energy Zone.

You can also see the Energy that will be
generated during your next turn.
Pikachu now has one Lightning Energy.
It can now use its attack, Gnaw.
battle_tutorial_energy_bench_message_001:
Energy can be attached to a
Benched Pokémon, too.
battle_tutorial_energy_bench_message_002:
By attaching Energy to a Benched Pokémon
you will be prepared to attack.
battle_tutorial_energy_bench_message_003:
Pikachu already has one Lightning Energy,
so it can use its attack.
battle_tutorial_energy_bench_message_004:
Attach a Lightning Energy to the Raichu on
your Bench.
battle_tutorial_energy_bench_message_005:
You attached an Energy to Raichu on your
last turn, so it can almost use its attack.
battle_tutorial_energy_bench_message_006:
Attach one more Energy to the Raichu and
use its attack.
battle_tutorial_energy_bench_telop_001:
Attach Energy to your
Benched Pokémon!
battle_tutorial_evolve_message_00100: Let’s try evolving a Pokémon during battle!
battle_tutorial_evolve_message_00200: Take a good look at the cards in your hand.
battle_tutorial_evolve_message_00400:
You can evolve the Pokémon that is shown
here with the correct Evolution Pokémon.
battle_tutorial_evolve_message_00500:
Charmeleon is the Pokémon in the
Active Spot.
battle_tutorial_evolve_message_00600:
Evolve Pokémon in play by putting Evolution
Pokémon from your hand on top of them.
battle_tutorial_evolve_message_00700:
Pokémon can have higher HP and stronger
attacks after evolving.
battle_tutorial_evolve_message_00800:
Even if a Pokémon evolves, it keeps all
attached Energy and any damage.
battle_tutorial_evolve_message_00900:
You can evolve as many Pokémon as you
want on your turn, except on your
first turn.
battle_tutorial_evolve_message_01000:
You can’t evolve a Pokémon on its first
turn in play or if it already evolved during
this turn.
battle_tutorial_goods_message_00100:
There are other types of cards that are
useful in battle besides Pokémon cards.
battle_tutorial_goods_message_00200: Take a look at the cards in your hand.
battle_tutorial_goods_message_00400:
Trainer cards are divided into Items and
Supporters depending on usage and effect.
battle_tutorial_goods_message_00500: This is the Item card, Potion.
battle_tutorial_goods_message_00600:
Playing this card will heal one of your
Pokémon’s HP.
battle_tutorial_goods_message_00800: Play Potion to heal Pikachu’s HP.
battle_tutorial_goods_message_00900:
You may play as many Item cards as you
like during your turn.
battle_tutorial_goods_message_01000:
Since Pikachu’s HP was healed, it
didn’t get Knocked Out.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_001:
Cards aren’t only for collecting. They can
also be used in battle.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_002: Take a look at the Pikachu card.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_003:
Pokémon have HP. When they lose all of
their HP, they are Knocked Out.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_004:
Here you can find a card’s attacks. With
these, you can attack your opponent’s
Pokémon and use the attacks’ effects.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_005:
You and your opponent’s Pokémon battle
one another as you try to Knock Out all
of their Pokémon one by one.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_006:
In a battle, you can use cards you’ve
collected to face off against your opponent.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_007:
In this guide, you can battle with cards
that have been set up for you.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_008:
The cards near you are your in-play zone,
and the cards on the other side are your
opponent’s in-play zone.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_009:
This is your Active Spot, and it’s where
your Pokémon battle using attacks.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_010:
Pokémon in the Active Spot are referred
to as Active Pokémon.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_011:
This is your Bench, and it’s where you put
Pokémon that can switch with your Active
Pokémon.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_012:
Pokémon on the Bench are referred to as
Benched Pokémon.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_014:
Your cards are placed here face down, and
you draw one on your turn.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_016:
You can have up to 10 cards in your hand,
and you use these cards during the battle.
battle_tutorial_introduction_message_017:
Starting in the next part of the guide, we’ll
go through the steps of a battle.
battle_tutorial_pokemon_tool_message_001: You have one Trainer card in your hand.
battle_tutorial_pokemon_tool_message_002: Let’s take a good look at it.
battle_tutorial_pokemon_tool_message_003:
This is the Pokémon Tool card,
Giant Cape.
battle_tutorial_pokemon_tool_message_004:
You can attach Pokémon Tools to your Active
Pokémon or to your Benched Pokémon.
battle_tutorial_pokemon_tool_message_005:
Once a Pokémon Tool has been attached to
a Pokémon, it remains attached until the
Pokémon leaves play.
battle_tutorial_pokemon_tool_message_006:
You can use as many Pokémon Tools during
your turn as you’d like, but each Pokémon can
have only one attached at a time.
battle_tutorial_pokemon_tool_message_007:
This card gives +20 HP to the Pokémon it’s
attached to.
battle_tutorial_pokemon_tool_message_008:
If your Pokémon is attacked on your
opponent’s next turn, it will be Knocked Out.
battle_tutorial_pokemon_tool_message_010:
Your Pokémon’s remaining HP is now 70, and
it looks like it’ll be able to withstand
one attack.
battle_tutorial_pokemon_tool_message_011: Let’s attach an Energy and end your turn.
battle_tutorial_pokemon_tool_message_012:
Because its HP was increased, Raichu wasn’t
Knocked Out.
battle_tutorial_preparation_message_0040:
Before starting the battle, let’s set up
your Pokémon.
battle_tutorial_preparation_message_0050:
First, put a Pokémon from your hand into
the Active Spot.
battle_tutorial_preparation_message_0060: Take a good look at the cards in your hand.
battle_tutorial_preparation_message_0070: You can play any Pokémon that says Basic.
battle_tutorial_preparation_message_0080: Place a Basic Pokémon in the Active Spot.
battle_tutorial_preparation_message_0090:
Once you’re done setting up your Active
Pokémon, next is setting up your Bench.
battle_tutorial_preparation_message_0100:
During a real battle, you have the option to
set up your Bench.
battle_tutorial_preparation_message_0110: For this guide, let’s practice setting it up.
battle_tutorial_preparation_message_0120:
You can put a Basic Pokémon here,
just like in the Active Spot.
battle_tutorial_preparation_message_0130:
Once you’ve set up your Pokémon,
go ahead and tap Start Battle.
battle_tutorial_preparation_message_0140: Now, you’re ready to begin the battle.
battle_tutorial_retreat_message_00100:
You can switch your Active Pokémon with
your Benched Pokémon.
battle_tutorial_retreat_message_00300: Take a look at Pikachu’s Retreat Cost.
battle_tutorial_retreat_message_00500: The Retreat Cost is one Energy.
battle_tutorial_retreat_message_00600:
Let’s retreat Pikachu and switch it 
with Raichu.
battle_tutorial_retreat_message_00700:
If you retreat, the Energy cost will be
discarded from that Pokémon.
battle_tutorial_retreat_message_00800: You can retreat once per turn.
battle_tutorial_retreat_message_00900:
You can still use an attack even if you
retreated during that turn.
battle_tutorial_special_condition_messag: Take a look at Grimer in the Active Spot.

It says that your opponent’s Active
Pokémon is now Poisoned.

Attacks can have all kinds of effects like this
apart from just damage.

This attack can make your opponent’s
Pokémon Poisoned.

Use Poison Gas to make your opponent’s
Pokémon Poisoned.

You made your opponent’s Caterpie
Poisoned.

Poisoned Pokémon take 10 damage during
Pokémon Checkup.

Pokémon will recover from Special
Conditions, such as Poisoned, when they
move to the Bench.

Apart from Poisoned, there are other
Special Conditions such as Paralyzed and
Asleep.
For more information, check out Tips.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_00100: You have one Trainer card in your hand.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_00200: Let’s take a good look at it.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_00300: This is called a Stadium card.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_00400:
When a Stadium card is in play, it has an effect
on both you and your opponent.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_00500:
You can play only 1 Stadium card from your
hand during your turn, and it stays in play.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_00600: Only 1 Stadium card can be in play at a time.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_00700:
When a Stadium with a different name is put
in play, discard the Stadium that was
previously in play and replace it.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_00800:
You can’t play a Stadium card with the 
same name as the Stadium already in play.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_00900:
This card makes attacks used by both
players’ Stage 1 Pokémon do +10 damage
to their opponent’s Active Pokémon.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_01000: Let’s take a look at this Charmeleon card.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_01100:
Because Charmeleon is a Stage 1 Pokémon,
we can apply the effect of Training Area and
increase the damage done by its attacks.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_01300:
We discarded the Stadium that your opponent
put in play and replaced it with Training Area.
battle_tutorial_stadium_message_01400:
Now, Charmeleon’s attack can Knock Out
Wartortle.
battle_tutorial_support_message_00100:
You only have one Trainer card in
your hand.
battle_tutorial_support_message_00200: Let’s take a good look at it.
battle_tutorial_support_message_00300:
This is the Supporter card,
Professor’s Research.
battle_tutorial_support_message_00400:
Unlike Item cards, you can only use one
Supporter card on your turn.
battle_tutorial_support_message_00500:
If you play Professor’s Research, you can
draw two cards from your deck.
battle_tutorial_support_message_00600: At this rate, Pikachu will get Knocked Out.
battle_tutorial_support_message_00700:
Play Professor’s Research and draw cards
from your deck.
battle_tutorial_support_message_00800: It looks like you drew a Raichu.
battle_tutorial_support_message_00900:
Let’s evolve Pikachu into Raichu and use
an attack.
battle_tutorial_top_training_btn_07:
Attach Energy to your
Benched Pokémon!
battle_tutorial_turn_end_message_00200: Let’s take a closer look at the Snorlax card.
battle_tutorial_turn_end_message_00450:
These are called Colorless Energy. The
symbols mean any type of Energy can be
used.
battle_tutorial_turn_end_message_00500:
When you can’t use an attack, tap the
End Turn button to end your turn.
battle_tutorial_turn_end_message_00600:
Energy will generate in your Energy Zone
during your turn.
battle_tutorial_turn_end_message_00700:
Attach a fourth Energy to Snorlax and use
its attack.
battle_tutorial_weakness_message_00400:
Let’s take a closer look at the opponent’s
Squirtle card.
battle_tutorial_weakness_message_00500:
Most Pokémon have a type that they’re
weak to.
battle_tutorial_weakness_message_00700:
Let’s use an attack by your
Lightning-type Pikachu.
battle_tutorial_weakness_message_00900:
You can do a lot of damage by attacking
Weaknesses.

pack_offer_ratio_caution_01:
When a pack is opened, the steps listed below will be carried out in sequence. (Further details follow.)

Step 1: Pack Selection
Step 2: Card Selection

About step 1: Pack Selection
Pack selection is the first selection process that is carried out.
In pack selection, a pack to be opened will be selected so that step 2, card selection, can occur.
Please see the Offering Rates tab to confirm the category names, offering rates, and number of cards in the packs that are generated.

About step 2: Card Selection
After the pack to be opened is decided in step 1, pack selection, step 2, card selection, is carried out.
In card selection, the cards that are actually generated will be selected.
The categories of cards offered and the offering rates differ for each pack. The number of cards in the packs may also differ. For example, if a “regular” pack is selected, cards will be generated as displayed in the categories, offering rates, and number of cards for “regular packs.” If a “rare” pack is selected, cards will be generated as displayed in the categories, offering rates, and number of cards for “rare packs.”

• Cards from packs not selected in pack selection will not be generated. For example, if a “regular” pack is selected, cards will be generated from “regular” packs. (Cards from “rare” packs will not be generated.)
• Please see the Offering Rates tab to confirm the specific probability rates for card selection.
• The offering rate displayed for each card is the offering rate after the pack category is decided in pack selection.
• The cards in a pack are selected one at a time.
• Booster packs that are available for a limited time only may be offered again after the availability period has ended.
• Cards available in this pack may also be available in packs added at a future date.
• The availability period and details are subject to change without warning.

Additional notes:
• It’s possible for the offering rate of cards included in the same pack to be different.
• It’s possible for the order of the cards in the results to differ from the order that the cards were actually selected in.
• It’s possible for the same card to be selected and offered two or more times in the same pack as duplicates.
• The offering rates are cut off after the third decimal place and may not equal 100% when added together.
• Actual offering rates have not been rounded up or down.
• Changes may be made, such as adjustments to card details or bans on certain cards from being used, as a result of error fixes or adjustments made to maintain a fair battle environment.
• The language of the cards will be the app’s selected language at the time a pack is opened.
• The language of cards already obtained will stay the same as it was at the time they were obtained and will not be affected if the app’s selected language is changed after they were obtained.

About “[Mst:Rarity v="RARITY_MSID_RR" ] or higher guaranteed” packs
• If the condition below is fulfilled, the next time a pack from the same expansion as the pack for which the condition has been fulfilled is opened, a [Mst:Rarity v="RARITY_MSID_RR" ] or higher card will be generated.

Condition: A [Mst:Rarity v="RARITY_MSID_RR" ] or higher card did not get generated after 12 consecutive openings of packs from the same expansion.
Note: Information related to fulfilling the condition, such as the current number of consecutive openings, or the number of openings remaining to fulfill the condition, will not be displayed.

• If the condition is fulfilled, the pack categories selected during step 1, pack selection, will change.
• During pack selection, the “[Mst:Rarity v="RARITY_MSID_RR" ] or higher guaranteed” pack category will be added but will not be the only category offered. It is possible for “rare” or “regular +1 card” pack categories to be offered instead.
Note: In that case, a [Mst:Rarity v="RARITY_MSID_RR" ] or higher card is still guaranteed to be generated.
• For more details, please see the “Offering Rates” tab.
